issues.description: StockIngredient.price type is inconsistent across artifacts. The problem statement UML declares StockIngredient.price as int and the UML lists the constructor as StockIngredient(String, int, int). The reference solution (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/StockIngredient.java) defines the field as 'private final int price' and the constructor parameter as int. The template (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/StockIngredient.java) however declares the field and constructor parameter as double ('private final double price' and StockIngredient(String, double, int)) and its getPrice() returns double. This mismatch between int (problem statement + solution) and double (template) will confuse students about the expected type and may cause compilation/type inconsistencies when they implement or run tests that assume the int-based API.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the price type consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fix (to match UML and the solution): change the template's StockIngredient.price to int (private final int price), change the constructor signature in the template to StockIngredient(String, int, int) and have getPrice() return int. Alternatively, if double is desired, update the problem statement UML and the solution to use double everywhere — but ensure all three artifacts (problem statement, template, solution) use the same type.
